newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says troops resume northern advance.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says troops resume northern advance.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops moved out of their camps in the northern Wanni region on two flanks on Monday in an attempt to converge at the key rebel-held town of Puliyankulam, military officials in the north said.

The troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air cover, eased out of northeastern Nedunkeni and northern Periyamadu at first light after consolidating these areas following an attack by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at the army's rear two weeks ago, they said.

"Troops resumed their advance further northward from the earlier held positions at first light today. Infantry troops are supported by columns of armour and artillery. The Sri Lanka air force aircraft are providing close air support," a Defence Ministry statement said.
"Satisfactory progress has been made so far and the terrorists are expected to resist the advancing troops," the statement added.
Military officials in the north said troops were aiming to get to Puliyankulam, 22 km (13.75 miles) north of Vavuniya.

Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a surprise attack on the military's rear near the northern government-held town of Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, delaying the main offensive.
They blew up a key bridge and an ammunition dump in what the Defence Ministry said was an attempt to wipe out the military's field headquarters.
Both sides are reported to have suffered heavy casualties in the fighting that lasted several hours.

Since then no major battles have been reported in the north though the troops and the separatists were involved in low-intensity warfare as the military tried to clear areas before resuming its advance.

Some 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru, or "Sure of Victory", last month through the brush jungle of the Wanni to open a crucial highway linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, a further 100 km (60 miles) north.
Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year.
The rebels have now set up base in the Wanni.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The clandestine rebel Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Monday that the military had launched a heavy shell attack in Puliyankulam area on Sunday. It did not give details.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as the international media has not yet been allowed in the war zone.

Sri Lanka President Chandrika Kumaratunga was quoted as saying by the state-run Daily News on Monday that there was a need to crush the rebels militarily before finding a political solution to the ethnic strife.
"We have little choice except fighting this rebel group militarily," Kumaratunga said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
